name: Kessler Kinetics VelocityFrame MkIV Sprint Leg
product_name: Kessler Kinetics VelocityFrame MkIV Sprint Leg
description:
The VelocityFrame MkIV is a full lower-limb replacement engineered around a carbon-composite endoskeleton with parabolic energy-return tendons that store kinetic energy during the compression phase and release it explosively at toe-off. Servo-assisted ankle joints respond to neural impulse in under 8 milliseconds, and the hollow-core tibia reduces total limb weight to 1.4 kg per unit. An integrated stride-optimization AI monitors gait in real time and micro-adjusts joint angles for maximum sprint efficiency.

The MkIV is the default leg for professional track athletes, courier runners, and anyone who needs to cover ground fast in the compressed transit corridors of the Shelf and Undercity. Street couriers call them Blades for the characteristic high-stepping gait they produce at full sprint.
installation_requirements: Full limb amputation or replacement surgery, certified neural interface socket, 48-hour calibration period
rejection_risk: Low — carbon-composite shell is biologically inert; neural socket requires standard immunosuppressant protocol
maintenance: Quarterly tendon-polymer tensioning; annual joint-bearing replacement; stride-AI firmware update recommended every 6 months
side_effects: Gait asymmetry if only one leg is replaced, requiring prolonged physiotherapy
Phantom limb feedback during high-speed operation reported in 12% of users
Stress fractures in residual femur if load distribution is miscalibrated
Hyperstimulation of motor cortex during stride-AI override events
cultural_context: Kessler legs are aspirational hardware in courier culture, where your legs are your livelihood. Owning a pair of MkIVs signals you've moved past desperation-grade gear and are serious about your craft.
known_users: Tier 3 working professionals with athletic ambitions
story_hooks: A courier's MkIV stride-AI has started rerouting her runs through a specific district for no logged reason — someone may have pushed a malicious firmware update
The underground racing circuit is offering a purse large enough to buy a Spire apartment, but the favorite to win is suspected of running black-market MkV prototype hardware
A Kessler engineer approaches the party claiming the MkIV's energy-return polymer was stolen IP — and the original inventor is somewhere in the Undercity
